problem: writeExportFile swallows every mkdir/writeFile failure: the catch only writes to stderr when KERYX_VERBOSE is set, and never rethrows or signals failure. runHistoryExport (line 122) then unconditionally prints 'exported N run(s) to <file>' (line 131) and leaves exitCode 0. Trigger: `keryx wiki history --runs --export /readonly-dir/runs.csv`, or an --export target that is an existing directory; outcome: success message, exit 0, no file written (the realpath catch at line 126 then also falls back silently to the typed path). Class scope: sites src/commands/wiki-history-export.ts:68 (the only swallowing catch in the change; the realpath catch at 126 is display-only and documented as such, the catch at 34 rethrows); enumerated by reading every catch in the diff.
impact: A user or script attaching the export to a review/flow journal is told it succeeded when nothing was written; the failure is only discoverable by enabling a debug env var.

problem: The JSDoc on collectRunRows says it 'Returns the runs oldest first, so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened', but the body only filters the result of listWikiRuns, which is documented and sorted 'newest first' (src/wiki/history.ts:495, :508). No reversal exists, so the comment asserts a behaviour with no code path.
impact: The next reader (and anyone relying on the export order) is misled about the row order; either the comment or the missing reverse is wrong, and the doc hides which.

problem: The command-label normalisation chain (collapse CR/LF, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copy-pasted three times: wiki-history-export.ts:49 (markdown branch), wiki-history-export.ts:56 (CSV branch, identical in the same function), and wiki-history.ts:47 (terminal listing). Only MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH was extracted, not the transformation.
impact: Any change to how labels are cleaned or clipped must be made in three places in sync; the two copies inside renderRunLine could have been one line above the if.

problem: renderRunLine takes four positional parameters including a boolean flag `markdown` that selects between two unrelated output formats, and two of the parameters (`at`, `pages`) duplicate fields of `run` (the caller passes `run.pages` straight through at line 119). Call site reads `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`. The RunExportFormat type already exists and is not used here.
impact: Callers must read the signature to decode the boolean and the redundant args; adding a third format means another flag or branch instead of a renderer per format.

problem: The catch around listWikiRuns discards the caught error: a generic message is thrown without `{ cause: error }`, and the bound `error` is unused.
impact: Whoever debugs a failed export sees only 'could not read the runs log' with no underlying errno/path, losing the context needed to fix it.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: The --export flags are documented three different ways in one change: HISTORY_USAGE here lists only `--export <file> [--format csv|md]`, while EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:13) and the wiki help (wiki.ts:925) also list `--since <date>` and `--command <text>`.
impact: A user reading the history usage line never learns the filters exist; the strings will keep drifting since each is maintained by hand.
